root_cause.text: In KVM’s SVM/AVIC handling, the CR8 write intercept bit in the VMCB was not synchronized with AVIC activation/deactivation state, so CR8 interception could remain enabled after AVIC was turned on and continue trapping guest CR8 writes indefinitely.
root_cause.evidence: The patch explicitly adds `svm_clr_intercept(svm, INTERCEPT_CR8_WRITE);` in `avic_activate_vmcb()` and `svm_set_intercept(svm, INTERCEPT_CR8_WRITE);` in `avic_deactivate_vmcb()`, and the CVE description states KVM “leaves the interception enabled after AVIC is activated” and that “CR8 will remain intercepted in perpetuity.”

intent_record.intent_summary: Enable AVIC activation to also clear the CR8 write intercept so CR8 accesses are handled correctly when AVIC is turned on.
intent_record.what: In avic_activate_vmcb(), the patch removes a blank line, keeps the existing clearing of AVIC/X2APIC bits and recomputation of avic_physical_id, and adds a call to svm_clr_intercept(svm, INTERCEPT_CR8_WRITE) immediately after enabling AVIC in int_ctl.
intent_record.how: At runtime, activating AVIC now also clears the CR8 write intercept for the vCPU, allowing CR8 writes to proceed without interception when AVIC is enabled. This changes vCPU execution behavior by aligning intercept handling with AVIC activation and avoiding unnecessary trapping on CR8 accesses.

intent_record.intent_summary: Re-enable CR8 write interception on AVIC deactivation for non-SEV-ES guests to restore correct virtual interrupt handling.
intent_record.what: In avic_deactivate_vmcb(), after clearing AVIC-related control bits and the physical ID mask, the code now checks `!sev_es_guest(svm->vcpu.kvm)` and, if true, calls `svm_set_intercept(svm, INTERCEPT_CR8_WRITE)`. This adds a new conditional intercept setup before the existing comment and subsequent logic.
intent_record.how: When AVIC is deactivated, non-SEV-ES guests will now have CR8 write interception re-enabled, ensuring the hypervisor regains control over guest TPR/priority writes that AVIC may have previously bypassed. SEV-ES guests are exempted from this added intercept path.

intent_record.intent_summary: Always intercept CR8 writes during VMCB setup to ensure correct handling regardless of APICv state.
intent_record.what: The conditional around `svm_set_intercept(svm, INTERCEPT_CR8_WRITE);` was removed, so `INTERCEPT_CR8_WRITE` is now always set in `init_vmcb()` instead of only when `kvm_vcpu_apicv_active(vcpu)` is false.
intent_record.how: At runtime, CR8 write intercepts will be enabled for all VCPUs during VMCB initialization, ensuring CR8 accesses are trapped regardless of APICv state rather than being selectively untrapped when APICv is active.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add a one-time warning when CR8 write interception occurs with APICv active.
intent_record.what: In `cr8_write_interception()`, the declaration and initialization of `u8 cr8_prev = kvm_get_cr8(vcpu);` was moved above the `int r;` declaration, and a new `WARN_ON_ONCE(kvm_vcpu_apicv_active(vcpu));` call was inserted before `cr_interception(vcpu)`.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the function now emits a one-time warning if it is entered while APICv is active, making an unexpected execution state visible for debugging. The logic of the CR8 interception itself is otherwise unchanged.

bic_trace_step.reason: The vulnerable construct is the lack of synchronization between AVIC enable/disable state and the CR8/x2APIC MSR interception setting. This snippet shows the new centralized handling that updates both together. In `avic_activate_vmcb()`, when AVIC is enabled it explicitly calls `svm_set_x2apic_msr_interception(svm, false)` for x2APIC mode and `svm_set_x2apic_msr_interception(svm, true)` otherwise. In `avic_deactivate_vmcb()`, it always re-enables interception with `svm_set_x2apic_msr_interception(svm, true)`. The callers were also changed from directly toggling only `AVIC_ENABLE_MASK` to invoking these helpers in both `avic_init_vmcb()` and `avic_refresh_apicv_exec_ctrl()`. This means the fix is already present, and the buggy state where CR8 interception could remain enabled after AVIC activation is not present in this code.
